div.head: Northu 55
div.ab: Sunnandæges cypingc we forbeodað æghwar ⁊ ælc folcgemot ⁊ ælc weorc ⁊ ælce lade ægðer ge on wæne ge on horse ge on byrdene.
Sunnandæges cypingc we forbeodað æghwar and ælc folcgemot and ælc weorc and ælce lade, ægðer ge on wæne, ge on horse, ge on byrdene.
Sonntags-Kaufhandel verbieten wir überall und jedes Volksversammlungs-Gericht und jede Arbeit und jeden Transport einer Ladung, sowohl zu Wagen, wie zu Pferde, wie als Tragelast.
We forbid Sunday trading everywhere, and every popular assembly [court], and all work, and all carrying of loads, whether by wagon or on horseback or as a burden carried.
Sunday market we forbid everywhere, and every public assembly and all work and all carrying [of goods], whether by wagon or by horse or on one's back.
We everywhere forbid trade on a Sunday and every public meeting and every type of labor and every type of transport, either by wagon or by horse or by carried load.
div.note: Liebermann compares I Cn 15 and EGu 7.1.

summagium ‘Last’ erklärt Q zu Rect 2; so Schmid 619 gegen seine Übs. ‘Reise’, was nicht zu byrdene passt. Vielmehr steht die dreifache Art der Beförderung bera a sjalfum, fara a skipi, bera a hrossi auch im Nord. Recht; Toller 605 Z. 1. Agsä. steht mon bere im Ggs. zu on wæne ferige ebd. 1152

Q on Rect 2 explains it as summagium ‘load’; so Schmid 619, against his own translation ‘Reise’, which does not suit byrdene. Rather, the threefold manner of transport bera a sjalfum, fara a skipi, bera a hrossi occurs in Norse law too; Toller 605 l. 1. In A.-S. mon bere stands in contrast to on wæne ferige ibid. 1152
